name: Crucible: Plex-mediasoitin
privacyPolicyText:
Crucible Privacy Policy
Effective November 13, 2026
https://midgarcorp.cc/crucible/privacy

What Crucible is
Crucible is a Plex client for iPhone and Apple TV made by Midgar Oy. It runs on your device and talks to plex.tv, to sign you in and find your servers, and to the Plex Media Server you choose. If you are on a Tailscale network it may also ask the computers on that network which one is your server, and only if you opt in does it talk to api.tailscale.com. From version 2.9 you can also connect Trakt and your own Seerr, described below; neither is contacted until you connect it. From version 2.10 you can also ask Crucible’s AI what to watch or for a written recap, described below; nothing is sent to it until you ask.

What we collect
Only what Crucible Pro needs: an anonymous Midgar ID and the records of your Crucible Pro purchases, described under The anonymous Midgar ID and Purchases below. Nothing about your library, your viewing or your Plex account reaches us, except what you send when you ask Crucible’s AI for something, described under Crucible’s AI below. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking SDKs. Midgar may publish aggregate statistics built from anonymous counts, such as weekly active installs, which never identify a person; Crucible sends no usage counts, so it adds nothing to them.

Your Plex account
You sign in with Plex’s own sign-in flow. Your Plex token is stored in the Keychain on your device and sent only to plex.tv and to your own servers. Plex’s privacy policy applies to your Plex account.

Your Tailscale token (optional)
If a server cannot be found on your Tailscale network by name, you may give Crucible a Tailscale API access token so it can read your device list. The token is stored in the Keychain on your device, sent only to api.tailscale.com, and can be removed at any time in Settings, Server, Tailscale Search.

Trakt (optional)
From version 2.9 you can connect your Trakt account in Settings, Integrations, Trakt. Nothing is sent to Trakt until you do. Once connected, Crucible sends Trakt (api.trakt.tv, run by Trakt, Inc.) what you play, when and how far you got, the titles you mark watched (and unwatched, if you turn that on), your ratings and your check-ins, each identified by the IMDb, TMDB or TVDB number your Plex server holds for it, and it asks Trakt for the scores it shows on detail pages and, for the Everything view in Statistics, for your watch history, which is kept only on your device. Plays from downloads wait on your device until you are online. Your Trakt sign-in is stored in the Keychain on your device, separately for each Plex account and Home profile. Disconnecting tells Trakt to revoke Crucible’s access and deletes what Crucible kept about your Trakt account on the device; your history on Trakt stays there. Midgar receives none of it. Trakt’s privacy policy applies to your Trakt account: https://trakt.tv/privacy.

Seerr (optional)
From version 2.9 you can connect a Seerr, Overseerr or Jellyseerr you or your server’s owner runs, in Settings, Integrations, Seerr. It runs on your own server, like Plex. To find it, Crucible asks the addresses your Plex server already answers at on your home network or your Tailscale network whether Seerr runs there. When you connect, Crucible signs in to it with your Plex token, or with an API key you type; it then sends Seerr the titles you request and asks it which titles are requested, downloading or available. Its session and any API key are stored in the Keychain on your device. Midgar receives none of it.

Your library and viewing history
Titles, artwork, watch history and the statistics built from it come from your Plex server and stay on your device, except for what you send when you ask Crucible’s AI (next section). A Year in Review poster is drawn on your device and leaves it only if you share it.

Crucible’s AI (optional)
From version 2.10 two features use an AI model that Midgar runs for Crucible, and only when you ask. What to Watch sends the sentence you type or dictate and, so that the model can choose among them, the titles, years, genres, lengths, ratings, age ratings and watched state of the films and series in your Plex libraries. Write a Recap, on a show’s Previously On, sends the name of the series and Plex’s descriptions of the last episodes you finished. Each screen says so before you ask. Nothing else is sent: no file names, no artwork, no Plex token and nothing about your Plex account. The request goes to Midgar’s service at api.midgarcorp.cc with your anonymous Midgar ID, which is how the service knows whether Crucible Pro covers the answer and counts how many answers that ID has asked for in a day. Midgar keeps that count and the time of each request, not what you asked or what was answered. To produce the answer, Midgar passes what you sent, without your Midgar ID, to Claude, a model run by Anthropic, PBC (United States), which under its commercial terms does not use it to train its models and deletes it within 30 days. Like any request, yours comes from your IP address, which Cloudflare’s request logs keep for up to seven days. With Crucible Server on your own computer, Previously On is written from your episodes by a model you choose, and none of this applies to it. The demo never makes these requests.

Episode guides
From version 2.8, about once a week Crucible downloads its episode guides, which say which episodes of a long show adapt the source and which are anime-only, from api.midgarcorp.cc. The request is the same for everyone: it carries nothing that identifies you, your library or what you watch, and the file is the whole guide, never the part for a show you have. Like any request, it comes from your IP address, which Midgar’s gateway uses only to limit how often one network can ask and which Cloudflare’s request logs keep for up to seven days. The guides are an open dataset at https://github.com/guitaripod/crucible-guides. The demo never makes this request.

The demo
The built-in demo runs a fictional library inside the app. It uses no network and no account, and leaving the demo forgets everything it stored.

Downloads
Offline downloads are saved on your iPhone and are not sent anywhere.

The anonymous Midgar ID
From version 2.4, the first time the app starts it asks Midgar’s server at api.midgarcorp.cc for an anonymous Midgar ID: a random identifier, and a random secret that proves the ID is yours. The server keeps the ID, a hash of the secret and the date it was created. The app keeps both in your iCloud Keychain, so the same ID follows you across your own devices and Midgar’s other apps. There is no name, email address, phone number, location or device name in it. On iPhone the app may ask Apple’s App Attest service to confirm that the request comes from a genuine copy of Crucible; we receive Apple’s attestation and nothing about you. You can have the ID and everything linked to it deleted by writing to marcus@midgarcorp.cc.

Purchases
Crucible Pro (lifetime or yearly) is sold through the App Store. Apple processes the payment; we never see your payment details or your Apple Account. Apple’s own notifications about Crucible Pro purchases (which product, the price, the dates, whether it renewed, lapsed or was refunded, the order identifiers and your App Store country) reach Midgar’s purchase ledger. From version 2.4, the app also sends the ledger the signed transaction record Apple has already issued, with your Midgar ID, so Crucible Pro is recognised on all your devices; the ledger keeps these records for as long as Apple’s financial records require. Version 2.4 contains no RevenueCat software. Earlier versions check and restore your purchase through RevenueCat (RevenueCat, Inc., United States), which receives a random app user ID and your purchase history for this app under its own privacy policy at https://www.revenuecat.com/privacy.

Diagnostics
A diagnostic log is kept on your device. It leaves your device only if you export and share it yourself.

Children
Crucible is not directed at children and does not knowingly collect information from anyone.

Changes and contact
If this policy changes, the new version appears here with its date. Questions go to marcus@midgarcorp.cc.
